Sony RM-EZ4 2-Device Universal Remote with Big Buttons If you have even the most bare-bones entertainment setup, you probable have quite a collection of remotes. They all have their uses but, for the times when you just want to turn on the TV and nothing else, it's nice to have a model like the Sony. Simple, small, easy to use and comfortable even for arthritic hands. Nice big buttons so you can see what to press even in low light.

Setup is a snap - just look up the brand of your TV and/or cable box on the supplied list, type in a four digit code, and you're done.

This is not a learning remote - it can only provide the functions that are pre-programmed into the unit (channel up/down, volume, channel entry via a number, channel recall and mute).

It uses two AA batteries that do not come with the unit. Build quality is very good - better than I expected given the price.

You can also get this in black if you purchase it at the store with the red bulls-eye logo. Amazon has a better price, but only offers it in silver.

There are little to no instructions regarding these headphones and I had to research the app that has to be downloaded and go to the Razer website to begin using. I was impressed with the noise cancelation especially. As an audiophile, I am very, very critical of sound and what is missing with these headphones is any kind of upper volume range or bass. The strongest plus to these headphones is the clarity of the music. Even with the lower volume and the lack of bass, the music is sharp and clear - something I have found gets lost with other brands. The noise cancellation is also a strength above others.

Overall, I would recommend if you’re not searching for heavily bassed or volumed headphones.

I currently have the antenna sitting on a window sill until The weekend comes and I can run the cable and mount it in the attic. Works great at 40 miles or less. Seagate Backup Plus 2TB USB 3.0 Desktop External Hard Drive for Mac (STCB2000900) A solid backup drive is essential for anyone who requires a decent backup system, and sometimes a RAID is not an option. I took the 2TB option and while it's a good drive (so far) the cost difference between it and the 3TB drive makes it a less-than-ideal choice.

This drive is set up as an external server backup drive which stands on a desk. My primary concern was power - would this drive have its own power supply or would it rely on power through the USB port? As it turns out, it does have its own power supply which in my opinion is a very good thing.

I do not have a Mac so the first order of business was to format the drive for ext3 (Linux). This process took 4 hours over USB 2. That's a long time! That said, it's a big drive, and there were no errors in the process. It also confirmed something that was not clear on the packaging - this drive will work just fine with Linux, even though it is pre-formatted for Mac. In addition, this is a relatively quiet drive which is a pleasant bonus.

I have not had this drive very long but so far there have been no issues with it. It seems to be reliable and stable, and that's what is most important when using a drive for backups.

Seagate has put together a nice storage and backup drive with this drive. ALthough preformatted for Mac it can be reformatted for Windows or Linux file systems if desired.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate Backup Plus 2TB USB 3.0 Desktop External Hard Drive for Mac (STCB2000900)

text_fidelity_a:
WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black I give this drive five stars for its size - its physical dimensions - because although I have the same quibbles about it as I do with all other external drives, its size is smaller than other 2.5" external hard drives I've seen, including the 1.5TB Seagate that I own.

In the 2.5" hard drive world - the drives that can run on just USB power - there are internal drives that you can pair with an external case and there are external drives that come in a case and with software - usually a Graphical User Interface (GUI) to help the layman back things up. Unlike the 3.5" hard drive world, capacities are larger earlier in the external devices, but somehow the casing and enclosed bridge (in this case SATA to USB) make the physical size larger than an internal drive with case. This one is still a little bigger, but really quite small. It's awesome, frankly. To have that much capacity in something you can store just about anywhere and you don't even have to mess around with a power cord.

What I don't like - and I complain about this with all external hard drives - is the included software that they want you to install to do backups, etc. As an advanced computer user, I think it's nonsense; even my mother should be able to use the drive without any software. Of course you don't have to use it. The thing that annoys me is that the drive - again, like all other externals nowadays - comes with a sleep timer set, in this case at 30 minutes, so I have to install the interface software to turn that off (necessary for my intended application), and then uninstall the software to get it off my system, but all software leaves a trace after its removal.

If this is your first USB 3.0 peripheral, be aware that the port on the drive is unlike any USB 2.0 port, and thus will require a different cable if you need one longer than the included ~1m cable. More industry stupidity, so they can overcharge for the first year or so. Look for a cheap one on Amazon so you don't have to run out to Best Buy and pay 10x too much. Interface cables are the one thing I believe in buying as cheap as possible - and thank God for Amazon in that respect.

One more note in response to another review: prices on non-solid state hard drives have been fluctuating a lot recently because of the Thai floods, and prices of electronics on Amazon always fluctuate. I typically check all prices before buying anything, but still end up buying from Amazon 99% of the time. I haven't seen Best Buy have a real deal in years. They make their money off lies that their employees tell you, either because they have been brainwashed in to believing said lies or because of commission. Do your own price comparison when the time comes to make a purchase.

The only thing I don't love about this drive is an industry problem that's not going away any time soon, and I have to just stop complaining about it (later). I give this a higher than average review because I was actually surprised - and impressed - with the physical size.
text_fidelity_b: WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black

When I got the laptop it came with a dongle that allowed me to connect the the ethernet cable through my USB port. The problem I had in the past was that I needed to use a device to read several types of SD cards, and the device is so large it can't really be plugged into my laptop USB ports. So, if you are looking for an ethernet to USB dongle, this one is highly recommended.

text_fidelity_a:
SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500) Compared to the Crucial 1TB M2 NVME I reviewed earlier, this Sabrent 512GB model benchmarks a little faster. And it works just fine on a PCI M2 adapter card, which are only a few bucks. (I bought the cheapest one available and it works.)

The NVME still offers much faster R/W speeds than other drives even when used with SATA 1 (as on my workstation). For example, the SSD I was using as my hard disk benchmarks at about 220MB/second. The Sabrent NVME on a PCI card benchmarks at about 1.5GB/second.

This time I experimented to see if I could get Debian Linux distro running on the NVME on my older workstation.

It took a few tries. Getting the OS to boot directly from the NVME was a no-go. Since the NVME is mounted on an adapter card, I had hoped it would trick the system into thinking it was just an ordinary SATA drive and boot from it. But that didn't happen.

So what I did was installed all the Linux OS EXCEPT for the boot folder on the NVME, and put the boot folder on the SSD HDD. So it boots from the SSD but the entire OS is on the NVME and runs from it.

Step one:

The partition manager in the Debian installer didn't want to partition the NVME at first.

So I bailed out of it and used GParted (Gnome disks utility couldn't do this) to "create partition table" and selected msdos as type. That wiped everything and turned the whole drive into unallocated space. From that point the partition manager worked.

Step two:

From the linux bootable USB installer I partitioned the SSD (not the NVME) with a primary partition labeled (to be mounted) as /boot. (You can make this partition most any size from a few GB on up---the boot files don't require a lot of space.) The remaining space I manually labeled as /msc.

I partitioned the NVME so the installer would put everything else on it, starting with / (root). You can simply make the whole NVME / root and the installer will take care of putting everything else on that drive, or you can do what I did and set up size-defined partitions for /home, /usr, and so on.

After installing the system, the installer asks where you want the bootloader GRUB installed. I selected the SSD.

It worked. The SSD does the booting to the NVME, which then runs the OS. And it did improve speed.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500)

Lasmex HB-69 Bluetooth Headphone Over Ear, Hi-Fi Stereo Wireless Headset Ergonomic Protein Earpads丨Noise Reduction丨Built in Deep Bass丨Foldable Telescopic Arms丨Wired Mode for Travel Work TV PC Mobile I have worked with a lot of headphones, in particular active noise canceling (ANC) phones though I have several pairs of regular phones as well. One of the things that really bugs me about headphones these days is that there is a strong emphasis on bass, and most “bass enhanced” headphones overdrive the bass to the point that it destroys the rest of the sound profile in the process. This pair is one of the very few I have used that boosts the bass and gets it right.

Well, let’s get right to it – the sound profile is the most important feature of any headphones. If the sound is off, music will sound terrible and even straight speech can sound weird. These headphones tout their bass response, and I was a little apprehensive at first. However, unlike most, the bass on these is not so overdriven that it gives me a headache or interferes with the midrange. This is very unusual. The bass is definitely strong, but what is interesting is that it is actually detailed and not just a pounding low-frequency noise. I can hear details in the bass range that I usually can’t hear. A bass guitar sounds like a bass guitar, not a heavy noise frequency that is lost in distortion even at lower volumes. Even more interesting is that the bass, while stronger than the midrange, does not overpower it and drown it out, and the midrange sounds right. The highs are nice and clear too, without being bitingly sharp. Overall, the manufacturer did a very good job getting the sound profile right. It’s not exactly balanced because of the enhanced bass, but the enhancement is done well enough to make music still sound very natural.

Another area of surprise for me is that these are quite comfortable to wear for a little while even though they’re on-ear phones and not over-the-ear phones. I usually prefer over-the-ear phones that fit snugly, and these are the opposite of that. They’re on-ear and fit lightly, though tight enough to stay on when I tilt my head down and they do not pinch. These still have a little sound leakage when the volume is turned up a little, though it isn’t too bad at all.

These are Bluetooth phones and I was able to get them to connect to my phone very quickly and easily. Reconnection is quick and effortless.

Would I change anything? Yes – I would make these a tighter-fitting over-the-ear headphone. However, that’s a personal preference.

Overall, I am hard-pressed to find much about which to complain with these headphones. They get the bass enhancement right and sound really good. If you like headphones with a good bass response but still sound good, these are a good choice to consider.

Anyway, this was the best $ I've spent in a long time. It holds the iPad without any sliding or moving (the device or the pillow) and it came in his favorite color. He loved it. I love it.

text_fidelity_a:
ibi - The Smart Photo Manager - Collect, Organize and Privately Share Photos & Videos from Smartphones, Cloud and Social Media Accounts - US Version IBI - THE SMART PHOTO MANAGER (US Version) makes it super easy to extract, back up, and share photos stored on my mobile devices. Instead of emailing cell phone photos that I want to share among electronic devices (an iPad Air (3rd Gen), a desktop PC, and a Samsung Galaxy cell phone), I can upload the photos to Ibi via a network connection with only a couple of clicks in the Ibi app.

No longer do I have to address an email, select and add the photos, send the email--and then reverse the process on a second device (open the email, download the photos, and save the photos to the device). All that’s necessary is to take the photos, open the Ibi app, choose “import photos”, select the photos, and hit the import button.

The photos are immediately uploaded to Ibi, and I can access them immediately on all of my other devices. There is no need to clutter up email or to consume precious storage space on my mobile devices, when all I want to do is share photos.

Ibi is extremely versatile. It allows you to sort and organize photos, and create Albums. It allows you to authorize certain people to email photos directly to Ibi. It allows you to set up different areas of Ibi for the use of individuals. It allows you to upload its contents to a PC or other even larger storage device by plugging in a USB cable (not included). It even allows you to stream your videos to a television set (using Chromecast or Roku apps).

Ibi is easy to set up, using Bluetooth. My iPad and my Galaxy phone both found the powered on (plugged in) Ibi in less than 30 seconds. Once set up, Ibi communicates via your home network’s Internet access. When your Ibi app is set up, click on Help, and download the complete user manual (a PDF file). The manual is easy to understand, and will enable you to get the most out of your Ibi.

Ibi is a small drive that easily fits on a bookshelf. It uses just one power cord. I really love this Ibi storage drive. It is simplifying my life.

+++++IMPORTANT NOTE: You should NOT choose “automatic backup” in the Ibi app Settings until you understand how the app works. With automatic backup enabled, Ibi will copy all of the photos stored on EACH mobile device, and you will probably get a lot of duplicate photos. For example, if you have been sharing and storing the same photos on an iPad and a cell phone, Ibi will copy the photos from each device. Worse, if you go into Ibi and delete the duplicates, Ibi will keep automatically adding the photos back as long as the photos still exist in storage on the two different devices.

You will probably want to use “automatic backup” when you first set up your Ibi. That way all of your photos will be automatically copied to Ibi to start you off. But you should turn “automatic backup” off before you start deleting duplicate photos. You will never have a problem with duplicate photos if automatic backup is turned off.+++++
text_fidelity_b: ibi - The Smart Photo Manager - Collect, Organize and Privately Share Photos & Videos from Smartphones, Cloud and Social Media Accounts - US Version

ELECOM Relacon Handheld Trackball Mouse, Thumb Control, 2.4GHz Wireless, Ergonomic Design, 10-Button Function with Smooth Tracking, Windows11, MacOS (M-RT1DRBK) I've bought and currently use both variants of the Relacon mouse. I'm putting this review on the wireless version.

Overall, 5 stars for the wireless with dongle, 3 stars for the Bluetooth. Unfortunately the Bluetooth one is a bit choppy with tracking, causing the pointer to jump to a random place on the screen often enough to be annoying. The dongle one doesn't have this issue for me. Otherwise they're identical in function and feel.

As a dedicated thumb trackball user since the early 90s, I love it! It is much better quality than any other ambidextrous thumb trackball I've optimistically tried over the years when looking for an alternative to the standard right (or rare left) dedicated handed thumb trackball. I have never been able to get comfortable or quick with finger trackballs, no matter how much I have wanted to or worked at it. Same with the Thinkpad trackpoint.

It is a physical relief to have a mouse that I can use in a neutral wrist position without having my hand or arm stretched out. It is especially nice to be able to transfer and use the mouse with my left hand when I need to type or do something else with my right.

I haven't installed the software or tried to remap the buttons. I just plug in the dongle or pair with Bluetooth, and Windows recognizes it. Since my displays are 1080 or smaller, I keep the speed or acceleration or dpi setting at 1 blink. The button is below the power switch, so I do accidentally tap it occasionally, but it's quick and easy to cycle back to 1.

The stand is more stylish than functional, and even with practice the mouse will sometimes slide right off, but at least it's included. Most of the time, I just switch it off and set the mouse on its side.
text_fidelity_b: ELECOM Relacon Handheld Trackball Mouse, Thumb Control, 2.4GHz Wireless, Ergonomic Design, 10-Button Function with Smooth Tracking, Windows11, MacOS (M-RT1DRBK)

Gone are the days of the corporate world only utilizing a briefcase..As this is a hip (maybe even yuppie or, millennial..?!) nice alternative to that!
TBH- this isn’t your kids “take to school” backpack unless, you’re adulting in school- it definitely has that feel for sure. This would be a perfect gift for a graduate to use in college or, one commuting to work in city or, to hip new job- it most definitely carries professional vibe look but, does it in a hip way! This would be ideal for anyone carrying more than just a laptop to/from work- as it has plenty of safe and secure room for multiple electronics or, camera equipment, and would be a dream for professional who travels for work.. it has the strap to attach it to luggage and makes navigating the airport a lot more hands free!
This comes in two sizes so it can fit the needs of your computer and equipment.Surprising, it can be worn just like a backpack- (Including strap to hold it secure) and yet, as you walk into office- it transforms into corporate world with ease! This is the smaller of the 2 sizes and yet, it feels roomy enough to fit your laptop and even better, there is still extra room for all creature comfort’s needed. My son uses this backpack in the larger size and the two sitting side-by-side are very comparable. I appreciate the fact that both are made with the same attention to detail and other then, the overall measurement- from what I can see- you will get the same bag and its integrity.

The outer layer feels almost neoprene-ish and I love how entire pack is formed/molded to have a harder exterior- it stand on its own which is so convenient to get things in and out as needed and also gives extra protection. The nice thing is- this looks like professional bag but, has all the smaller sections and creatures comforts that are appreciated in a backpack. I love the front pocket- great for wallet/ID/airline info/ Cel phone/keys/etc.. all in there neat little spot. Im telling you, those with OCD will love this bag!!

The bonus feature with this bag- is the usb charging port. NO! This isn’t a Tesla magic bag.. that magically provides power. You must add a battery charge pack to the inside outlet. No, we did not use this flying with the airlines yet as, I’m hoping there will be no issue with the extra battery supply? ( I know there were issues with batteries combusting mid flight… I’m guessing this is not one of them?! )
If you are looking to get or give a nice “corporate style” bag with all the bells and whistle’s…this is hands down worth it and one that I stand behind and feel, will not disappoint !
*The only suggestion I have for manufacture would be: include a battery boost pack with the sale of the backpack and have this item be all inclusive.. it would also assure your battery pack would fit and show where/how it fits/connects.. and keeps things simple. Lexar E-Series 128GB Micro SD Card 2 Pack, microSDXC UHS-I Flash Memory Card with Adapter, 100MB/s, C10, U3, A1, V30, Full HD, 4K UHD, High Speed TF Card I've owned a few Lexar USB drives and Micro USB drives in the past and they have all had good quality and performance. I've attached the crystal diskmark performance below, but keep in mind that I am using the built-in microsd reader in my computer so speeds may vary as the reader has just as much to do with these benchmarks as the memory card itself.

I don't have any equipment that really stresses the microsd too much. The cameras that I have, while they can record up to 4K at 30fps, have generally had no problem writing to a U1 microsd. The Lexar, which I keep in my Osmo Pocket, is no exception, it has not had an issue recording video.

There is one key thing to point out about Lexar storage media that I've experienced in two of my past devices and that is the built-in expiration or time-bomb (if you don't agree with this philosophy). Lexar seems to have the philosophy that keeping your data intact is the most important when it comes to these products. Solid-state storage media has a theoretical limit to how many times they can be written to. Once that is hit, the media will be permanently damaged. Lexar has written into their firmware, a hard limit that once you write a certain number of times to their media, it will become read-only, keeping your data intact, but the storage unusable from that point on.

While I've experienced failed media in the past, I really only had this behavior with Lexar. I have to say, it did save my wife from losing the pictures on her phone if the card failed instead of becoming read-only.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar E-Series 128GB Micro SD Card 2 Pack, microSDXC UHS-I Flash Memory Card with Adapter, 100MB/s, C10, U3, A1, V30, Full HD, 4K UHD, High Speed TF Card

Tv was pretty easy to wall mount and looks beautiful on the wall!

The sound is really good, I don't even need to use a soundbar with this tv! I love the acoustic auto calibration- you sit on the couch and start it- it blasts sound in several directions thru the speakers and the mic on your remote picks it up and adjusts the sound based on where you're sitting and what kind of room you're in. Another amazing sound feature is the bluetooth they added in on this one, you can use bluetooth headphones with this!

The motion on it is pretty decent, it has enhanced motion features you can turn on for say sports and gaming but for regular tv watching, you won't want them on. This tv can adjust the brightness based on the lighting in the room which is impressive.

Tv switches between apps and thru the apps extremely smoothly! Overall I think this is an amazing tv packed in at a really modest price that won't send you to the poor house! If you have a higher budget and want top of the line, check out Sony's 90J series which is a step up from the 80J. But on a budget- this tv will certainly make you happy, it's an amazing machine!

text_fidelity_a:
CableMod C-Series Classic ModMesh Sleeved Cable Kit for Corsair Type 4 RM Black Label/RMi/RMX (White) I purchased these for the RM650x in my new build. to clean up the appearance of my case, as the default Corsair cables are serviceable but neither flexible nor visually appealing. Do I have a fancy case? It's a Fractal Define Mini C, so, sorta. Do I have a side window? No. Will anyone ever see the interior of this case aside from me and randos and I'm flexing on? Certainly not.

Why get cables like these? Call it an eccentricity. I don't like chaos hiding right out of sight. Sure, the Mini C would have the outward appearance of a stocky monolith of unalloyed order, but inside there would be a twisting madness of PVC and copper, heaving silently against the surface. There would be no evidence of it, sure, but I would know.

I would know.

So anyway, I purchased these to extend the relentless teleology of the IC into the broader world, and to this end I was successful. The cables are much more flexible than the default ones and the paracord is an interesting contrast against the typical circuit boards and enameled aluminum panels. They are a bit pricey for what you get, that's definitely the case - you might be better served by getting a different brand or shorter extensions rather than the full PSU set. I just happened to have the money for the CableMods.

Caveats: if you are using velcro ties inside the case, then you have to be careful with the ModFlex, as the hook-side can pull threads from it. I presume ModMesh, being nylon, would not have that issue. to get around it, I used rubber/silicon bands, since unlike zipties they can be removed and adjusted relatively easily.

Would I recommend them? If you have a side-window or transparent case, they are a definitely aesthetically on point. ModFlex or ModMesh, either should be suitable. If not, unless you too are eccentric, it probably isn't worth it. The improvement in airflow and the reduction in strain on the components are minimal so long as you are implementing reasonable cable management techniques. I'm still happy I purchased them though, since I'm pretty sure I'll be able to use them in the next two-three builds and they did make it a bit easier to get everything where I wanted it.
text_fidelity_b: CableMod C-Series Classic ModMesh Sleeved Cable Kit for Corsair Type 4 RM Black Label/RMi/RMX (White)

Amazon Basics Wireless Keyboard with Touchpad for Smart TV - US Layout (QWERTY) This AMAZON BASICS WIRELESS KEYBOARD (with Touchpad for Smart TV - US Layout (QWERTY)) has the easiest setup I’ve ever encountered for a wireless device. You insert 2 AAA batteries (included) into the keyboard, plug the USB radio receiver into a USB port on your Smart TV, and you’re instantly connected. If for some reason you aren’t automatically connected, you just hit Esc-K to connect.

The keyboard works with my Samsung QLED Q7F Smart TV. Not all of the function keys work with every screen--for example, the keyboard’s “Mute” button does NOT mute the TV--but that’s normal for generic controllers like this one that are intended to work with many different wireless devices.

The keyboard does everything that my Samsung remote does (for example, switches between apps, sources, calls up the TV settings menu), although it takes a bit of experimentation to learn how to use it. The direction keys near the touchscreen allow you to navigate the TV screen and everything else. If you go to the TV’s Internet area, the touchscreen activates and you see a big arrow cursor that works like a mouse.

The keyboard does the one thing that I really wanted. It has a Search button that allows me to search for TV shows, movies, etc. by typing on the keyboard, instead of by navigating around letter-by-letter on an onscreen letterpad. The keyboard does NOT work when I’m using Roku for searches, but that’s normal because the keyboard is designed to connect directly to a Smart TV (not to the TV’s connected accessories).

The keyboard does feel cheap, and I wouldn't want to use it as a computer keyboard. However, it's fine for my occasional use as a Smart TV keyboard.

NOTE: The wireless adapter is stored at the upper left of the box, inside the folded cardboard. The batteries are on the right.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Wireless Keyboard with Touchpad for Smart TV - US Layout (QWERTY)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 1350LMT 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)) I drive in and around the Boston area, where none of the streets run north/south or east/west, every other intersection is a rotary, and a wrong turn down a one way street can take you an hour to correct.

The Nuvi is slightly better than trying to drive with a map on your steering wheel. I have been using mine for awhile now, and it mostly gets me where I want to go.

The problem is mostly how it does it. As many have already noted, there is no easy way to get it to show you alternate routes. And out of the city, especially, the route it gives you can be full of surprises. Take you off the highway and onto a dirt road for no reason whatsoever surprises. That happened to my husband on his way to a job in Hartford.

And forget trying to get around traffic. I was using it to get home from a doctor's office and saw that there was a ton of traffic on the route it was giving me through Harvard Square, so I turned toward another way home - one I do not know as well, but I know it is possible to get home that way - expecting the Nuvi to tell me it was recalculating and give me my next turn.

It did so, and I turned and followed the directions each time as it - get this - took me into the Harvard Business School parking lot and then out onto a one way street that put me on a no-turning-back 100% committed course to the traffic in Harvard Square.

Thanks, Nuvi.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 1350LMT 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer))

text_fidelity_a: TIMMKOO MP3 Player with Bluetooth, 4.0" Full Touchscreen Mp4 Mp3 Player with Speaker, Portable HiFi Sound Mp3 Music Player with Bluetooth, Voice Recorder, E-Book, Supports up to 512GB TF Card (Black) I have an AGPTEK MP3 player, and it's not bad, but I can't read the dim, microscopic display, especially outside.  I was looking for something equally affordable with a display I could see and navigate without glasses.  In this respect, the Timmkoo excels.  The display is fantastic.  The BlueTooth 4.2 does a nice job of feeding the sound to my Bose wireless earbuds, and is easily connected. I like the BlueTooth screen, which is very easy to use.  The other day, I absentmindedly walked away from the Timkoo by about 20 feet, and realized I was still getting my music loud and clear.  I can walk around with the player in my pocket and listen, where I have to hold my other player in front of me or it cuts in and out. text_fidelity_a:
Acer C720 Chromebook (11.6-Inch, 2GB) **Discontinued by Manufacturer** These are pretty much the perfect laptop for kids (and adults too if they don't want to download or install any personal programs). The Google App store has just about every type of app/program you could want. These don't have a DVD drive and you can't download programs unless they are from the App store. It's a good way of keeping your machine safe from malware attacks. No need to purchase and renew antiviral software. The screen is clear and bright, and the keyboard works really nicely. The sound from these is much better than the sound on my much more expensive laptop. Overall, the size and functionality of the Chromebook is much better than my new Windows 8.1 laptop.

My kids were able to get started immediately with minimal help from me to download some apps they like, get their e-mails set up and started using these Chromebooks immediately. I personally am not nuts about having only Google Chrome as my internet browser, thus I don't own my own Chromebook, but for my kids purposes (mainly games and schoolwork) the Chromebooks work out great. I really like how easy and smoothly they work. They are faster than my laptop and I do find that appealing, but I like being able to use a DVD drive and to be able to download what software I might want from the internet.

Printing is possible from the cloud and set up to do that is not difficult. Everything is easy........almost too easy. You can't store any data on the computer itself, only in the cloud. But, I'm not worried about any personal information being accessed by nefarious types because there's really nothing to access.

We've had these Chromebooks since Christmas and they are still working fine with no problems whatsoever.

UPDATE: 2.28.15 - My daughter brought it to my attention that these chromebooks do not have a "delete" key. Interesting.

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Move Style Edition, Black – Wireless Bluetooth Headphones with Superior Sounds Quality, Long Battery Life, Ultra-Light and Comfortable Wireless Headphones, 3.5 mm Jack Connector Included First I like sound! I'm an audiophile at heart but in my life now I'm an audiophile on a BUDGET! These are my first bluetooth speakers. More on that in a minute.

I was looking for on ear bluetooth speakers with a budget of about $50 to $60 and was set on waiting for a sale on the JBL EB45T but then saw these recommended on the wirecutter website (a pretty good review site in my opinion)

There is nothing wrong with these, but nothing really right about them either. They have a nice neutral sound that you can listen to for a long time. For movies and youtube on my computer, they are great. But there is nothing in the sound that is going to wow you either. Trust me if there was something actually wrong with the sound, I'd be telling you. You can listen to these for a long time without ear fatigue. If you are looking for lots of rumble for movies, these probably aren't the right phones for you. But if your movie listening requirements are more modest then these work well for that. For casual background music, podcasts, audiobooks, they will work really well for that.

Isolation is not great. I think the plastic is thin so a certain amount of noise gets in. I wanted to be able to hear a little bit of background noise, things going on in the house, but these push my limit for how much I want to hear. Even though they were open-back my Sennheiser HD-229 did a better job with isolation because of the design of the pad.

Comfort isn't bad and for my ears, the ear cup size is just about right size. I wish the earpieces swiveled a bit more but for my head, they swivel just enough. . They have a left and right and the cups swivel so little that if you have them on the wrong way you will notice.

Bluetooth... These are a pain in the backside on Win 7. When I want to use them I have to go and delete the previous pairing, pair them again and then go to the control panel and set these to be used for output. For movies on the computer, they get out of sync. I even set my movie player (Pot Player which I highly recommend) to use the Bluetooth headphones and they still get out of sync with the audio. I don't know if it's the player, the USB Bluetooth adapter, Windows 7 or some combination of them together.

I like that they can be used with a wire as well as with bluetooth. The controls are a little small, as mentioned by others but I don't have trouble working them.

I also tried the JBL EB45T Bluetooth headphones, which cost almost twice as much, at Target and these sound better overall. The JBL might have had better highs, a little punchier bass but these are more cohesive across the frequency range with nothing tweaked to make them sound 'better'.

Summary: I don't have any other Bluetooth headphones to compare these to but I think most people would be very satisfied with these at this price point for general use. If however, you are looking for audiophile on a budget, it's not here.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Move Style Edition, Black – Wireless Bluetooth Headphones with Superior Sounds Quality, Long Battery Life, Ultra-Light and Comfortable Wireless Headphones, 3.5 mm Jack Connector Included

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor This little device does a lot.
While it is sort of a smart watch, it sort of isn't, too. But what it does, it does well.

The good:
- Excellent selection of watch faces, including cute, clever, big, pretty, etc. You can change your face every day to match your clothes if you want.
- If I understand correctly, you can use it with other services, like Spark People.
- measures pulse, steps, miles. Tracks exercise on demand.
- motivates in numerous ways. Reminders to stand up, encouragement to finish your goal steps for the hour, challenges, even "travel" challenges that are longer term.
- large userbase. You can network with more of your friends on Fitbit than on any other fitness watch.
- big face without losing attractiveness
- large variety of replacement bands available from third parties, some very pretty.
- Can be used with many other fitness applications.
- Detects sleep surprisingly accurately
- Lots of settings options
- A decent number of apps available
- Handles the shower well
- If you never have to take it off except to charge, it's harder to lose it.
- Charges very quickly
- The charger is an awesome design and easy to use
- You can always have your alarms with you so you never miss them.

The irritating
- All changes have to be made through the app.
- If you don't sync often enough, it loses your data
- Sync can take a long time.
- The battery life is considerably shorter than I expected. It's about 2 1/2 days if I have constant sync turned off.
- Don't even bother with constant sync unless you're willing to take it off to charge a lot.
- All the music apps are paid

All in all, though, the pros are big and the cons are small. Enough that it still warrants a 5 star review.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers For years, I used the keyboard kindle after it first came out and loved the "classic" look of the page so much. After replacing it several times due to screen issues, I finally made the switch to the paperwhite with some skepticism, thinking the back-light would make it into yet another screen I look at. I was pleasantly surprised that even the brighter settings still look like a page, and I can turn it all the way down for the same effect as my older model kindle. Plus, I don't need to bother anyone with a light anymore when I read in bed, in the car at night, etc.

Paying a bit extra for no ads was worth it, and I enjoy the drawings that serve as screensavers. The home page is not my favorite - I would prefer to default to my library list instead of wading through recommendations, etc. - but it's not that much of a hassle to tap over to the library screen. When I'm reading a book, it automatically opens to the page I left off on just like my old kindle.

I only vaguely miss having the 3G function my old kindle had because I used to live out in the boonies with limited internet access. However, the WiFi has been generally sufficient and now I just make sure I download a few books before I travel.

Overall, the kindle has definitely revolutionized the way I read since it first came out when I was in high school. text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link Deco AXE5400 Tri-Band WiFi 6E Mesh System(Deco XE75) - Covers up to 2900 Sq.Ft, Replaces WiFi Router and Extender, AI-Driven Mesh, New 6GHz Band, 1-Pack Honestly, I wish I had a tried a Wifi6 mesh system sooner. This is NIGHT AND DAY difference over my previous D-link router + extender. I thought that since both my router and extender were D-link and had the ability to "communicate" with each other, it would work pretty well, but honestly even when it "worked" it was pretty laggy, and outside on the porch it would drop to single digit speed tests, if anything at all (forget about streaming for backyard movie nights!).
This system, however, is incredible. I'm now getting nearly 200mbps outside where I used to have nothing, and in most of my house I'm hitting my maximum 250mbps that I'm paying for with my internet service. Everything responds quickly and smoothly, and I love the control that the TP link system gives over what devices are connected (it alerts me when a new device connects!) and being able to set restrictions and time limits as well!
The one downside, however, is the physical ports. For starters, there are only 3 of them per unit. If you use ethernet backbone to connect them, that leaves only one on the primary node (one for the internet connection to the modem, and the other going to the second node- only one available for anything else). In my case, I have an ethernet cable going to my desktop for work (the most reliable connection), and another going into a telephony system. The 3 port limitation would have been difficult if I hardwired the satellite, but thankfully I didn't have to. The wireless mesh over 6Ghz actually works quite well so far so I managed with only the 3 ports on the primary one.
That being said, at first I had a major issue with the speed on my hardwired connection. The desktop claimed to only connect at 100mbps. Meanwhile, if I turned on wifi I was pulling 250mbps. That can't be! Many chats to customer support and we couldn't figure it out until I switched ports on the Deco and now I'm getting the full 250 over ethernet. I don't know if it was the port having trouble or just reseating the wire that did it, but I never had that on my previous D-link router, and it had more ports too in case I needed them.

In a nutshell, I got it working, and for what it is supposed to do, I'm VERY very impressed at the performance. But the hardwire hiccup and limitation in number of ports available makes this a 4 instead of 5 star review.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link Deco AXE5400 Tri-Band WiFi 6E Mesh System(Deco XE75) - Covers up to 2900 Sq.Ft, Replaces WiFi Router and Extender, AI-Driven Mesh, New 6GHz Band, 1-Pack

CoolBELL 17.3 Inches Convertible Laptop Messenger Bag Shoulder Bag Backpack Oxford Cloth Multi-Functional Briefcase for Men Women Laptop/MacBook (Blue) First and foremost, I need a convertible backpack which allows for transport - all materials needed for the long days on campus (grad student). In addition, I need the professional aspect to function as a briefcase. Solely on those points, this bag fits the bill. (BTW - no discount or freebie here for this review - I paid for this!)
PROS:
1. Material: feels and looks professional, good color, seems at the very least to be water repellent
2. Zippers: seem strong enough, especially when loaded - two of them house the briefcase handles
3. Padding: quality - on the backpack straps and particularly the section directly meant for the computer
4. Compartments: although the pictures do not necessarily show this, there are zippers on the outside, and inside, a pocket with divisions for pencils/pens/highlighters.

CONS:
1. Backpack adjustable straps: are on the lower part not allowing for easy adjustment while on your back
2. Lower connection backpack straps: hidden - cannot see whether sewn in well or not
3. Strap to hold computer in place: oddly long, which would allow for movement and sliding around, something you don't want your computer to do when inside
4. No compartment/pocket for a water bottle (my pet peeve)
5. PRIMARY (HUGE) ISSUE: Backpack straps which rest on upper trapezoids (left and right) are situated in a very uncomfortable position when fully loaded. I'm unsure if it's the angle or the placement, but the straps are too close to your neck and would cause pain. Primarily for this reason, I'm returning the backpack. Sad because even with the other cons (more annoyances than anything else) if it were not for this one, I would've kept the backpack because the pros outweigh the cons.

Pictures: It's important to see how a backpack will perform in my daily life. Therefore, the pictures provide a sense of how much stuff this can carry, with the contents both packed and unpacked.

Contents: Lenovo ThinkPad T460 in neoprene case, keys, 1 1/2" loose-leaf binder, yearly planner, scientific calculator, computer power cord, small cosmetic case, large cosmetic bag which houses pens/pencils/highlighters/usb drive/mouse/headphones and wallet.

Final thoughts: if only used as a briefcase/shoulder bag, this may be for you. However, if the primary purpose is to function as a backpack, good luck. I think another reviewer mentioned the oddly-placed backpack straps, but sadly, I ignored that advice.
In addition, cannot ascertain the strength of the shoulder strap as I didn't want to break the seal, but it is pictured.

text_fidelity_a:
Elgood Tabletop Vacuum Cleaner with Cleaning Brush,Eraser dust Vacuum USB Charging,Best Desk Vacuum No Dead Angle Cleaning(Green) Like many single guys I have various pockets of dust scattered around my place. My desk, behind the computer towers and monitors where all the cords are piled up is one of the worst. So a handheld vacuum to clean all those nooks and crannies sounded like a good idea. Sadly, this is not the portable vacuum that I am looking for.

A few design flaws were obvious as soon as I took this out of the box and started charging it. There is no stand or holder for the vacuum so it has to sit directly on the brushes you've just been cleaning with. The light indicating when the vacuum is charging/fully charged is pinhole size, barely visible from any distance. So I had to go pick it up and squint at the light to see if it was charged up. The little brush for cleaning the inside of the vacuum is one more tiny thing to keep track of and is easily lost.

Even more flaws became obvious as soon as I tried to use the vacuum. With the nozzle on I tried to clean the back of my desk where all the computer wires are. The nozzle immediately jammed up on hair and dust balls. That area is still as dusty now as it was before I tried to vacuum it. Next I tried cleaning some flat surfaces. The brushes pushed the dust back and forth while barely vacuuming any of it up. I put my hand across the bottom of the brushes and could not feel any suction at all. When I put my finger right into the center hole that the dust was supposed to be scooped up into, I could barely feel a tiny amount of suction. I still very much like the idea of a handheld vacuum but I very much do not like this one and cannot recommend it to anyone.
text_fidelity_b: Elgood Tabletop Vacuum Cleaner with Cleaning Brush,Eraser dust Vacuum USB Charging,Best Desk Vacuum No Dead Angle Cleaning(Green)

text_fidelity_a:
Donner Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.2 Earphones with 4 Mic Clear Calls, 12mm Drivers, App for Custom EQ, 32H Playtime, Fast Charging, Transparency - Dobuds ONE, Blue Budget-priced earbuds are complicated to review because, in my experience, all $200 earbuds sound significantly better than all $50 earbuds, but there is still a lot of demand for value-priced "good enough" products. I do own a couple of $200 earbuds and they do sound noticeably richer and clearer than these $40 earbuds. However, when I'm out jogging or traveling (eg airplane or train) or listening to voice podcasts, having the absolute best sound quality isn't really important to me. In those situations, features are more important to me, like active noise cancellation, equalization, good volume, good battery life, and easy access to the features. I'd rather use cheap earbuds that I don't mind losing somewhere along the way.

These earbuds have average quality sound for the $40 price. Where these Donner earbuds beat the competition is the features. I've never owned $40 earbuds with app control before. The user manual has a QR code to let you download the app. The QR code did not work, but I did find the "Donner Control" app in the Google Play app store and the app works fine on my Android phone. The app lets me pick from pre-programmed equalization settings or design my own. Adjusting the equalization for different types of music makes a significant difference in audio clarity. The app also lets me choose from 3 active noise cancellation modes. These features don't work as well as in $200 earbuds, but these are $40 earbuds and most $40 earbuds don't have any of these features or any app at all. You can control some of these features with the confusing set of triple-tap commands on the earbuds, but I can never remember those and would rather just tap the picture in the app.

The app also lets you download firmware updates from Donner. None was available when I checked, but this could be a great way for them to refine the features of the earbuds or even add new features. They ask you to give them your email address and create an account when you open the app, but I did not and the core features of the app still work OK.

Battery life for these earbuds is good for this price range (6 to 8 hours, depending on whether or not you use ANC). As with most budget-priced wireless earbuds, maximum volume is OK but not great. Bass is above average for the $40 price. Static noise is very low. The Bluetooth connection has been very stable for me, even when I'm 30 feet away from my phone or in a different room in the house.

I can't give these earbuds 5 stars because I can easily buy better sound quality with more money, but these are solid 4 stars for value at the current $40 price.
text_fidelity_b: Donner Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.2 Earphones with 4 Mic Clear Calls, 12mm Drivers, App for Custom EQ, 32H Playtime, Fast Charging, Transparency - Dobuds ONE, Blue

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom GO 2535TM World Traveler 5-Inch Bluetooth GPS Navigator with Lifetime Traffic & Maps and Voice Recognition (Discontinued by Manufacturer) The TOMTOM GO2535 TM WTE is quite attractive with a large screen and smooth appearance but because of its size, this is a heavier GPS than many others. A magnetic plug attaches the power supplies either to a computer with its USB plug or to a car with its accessory power plug. As with most GPS devices, no "home" DC power supply is included. I have found the car mount to be great, easy to attach and remove from the windshield with a simple turn. My only complaint with the mount is that it takes some work to direct the device to a visible position and I fear that it will not last as long as the GPS. The magnetic plug slips into a cutout in the mount, allowing it to remain in position so the GPS can quickly be inserted or removed for safekeeping.
As for the functionality of the GPS, it has some problems, thereby preventing me from giving this a 5 star review. I'll simply list the Pros and Cons.
Pros:
Start up time is quick and option to start from last destination can save time if the satellite connection is delayed.
Menu options are easily learned even if at first they seem to include extra steps.
Responds quickly to need for alternate route when a turn is missed.
Ease in moving through functions on screen.
POIs are expansive and easy to discover
Map identifies a location I frequent which is not identified by any other GPS I've used.
Identifies traffic light cameras adequately. Have yet to receive speed camera warning.
Voice commands are intuitive and a little printed card is included if you're in need of prompting.
Connectivity to my Mac is easy and the option to automatically check for updates can save time.

Cons:
Speed is not always accurate. Often has my car going at 10 mph less than actual speed.
When setting a new destination, I've been unable to change the state unless I do it using the voice command. This may be possible, but I haven't had the time to investigate. Since I'm in a metropolitan area and may venture through 2 states and the District of Columbia in less than an hour, it's important for me to access the individual states.
When using phone through the GPS, although I can hear the conversation with no problem, the person on the other end of my call can't hear me clearly. Every time I've used it with a phone, the call has been dropped. I've never had a call dropped otherwise with my phone or other Bluetooth capable device.
Does not recognize voice commands at times.
Voice prompts are very frequent and I'd love to be able to reduce them but not turn it off.
Seldom comes up with the routes I usually take, even with a second try after selecting the Change Route option.

All in all, this is a good GPS navigation device and the lifetime updates are a definite advantage. I haven't traveled the wold with it, but will update my review as necessary with observations internationally. I do know the maps are on the device because I saw them when I performed the update last week and couldn't figure out how to get back to the USA on the device. For some reason, TOMTOM put me in the UK even though I'm registered in the USA and confirmed that selection.

What's interesting is that I still prefer my 3-year-old Navigon for its ease of use, accuracy and lovely displays, with two exceptions. I do not care for their customer service or necessity to download map updates to the device's SD card instead of doing a direct update on a Mac. This TOMTOM excels there and it comes in a very definite second for any GPS I've used. When the time comes for my beloved Navigon to bite the dust, I feel confident that I'll still be happy with this TOMTOM.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom GO 2535TM World Traveler 5-Inch Bluetooth GPS Navigator with Lifetime Traffic & Maps and Voice Recognition (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
FDY MP3 Player, MP3 Player with Bluetooth5.0, 32GB Portable Music Player with FM Radio/Recorder, HiFi Lossless Sound Quality, 2.4Inch Touch Screen Mini MP3 Player for Running, Expandable 128GB TF When I opened the package containing this MP3 player, I was amazed at how small it is. But immediately became delighted at its perfectly small size. It is not the size of a small cellphone, but rather like what should have naturally occurred if an iPod shuffle mated with an iPod Nano. Perfect size and perfect function.

As the product description does not list or show the size of this MP3 player I list them here:

Length: 2 3/4 inches Width: 2 inches Thickness: 3/8 inch

Yes, small, but a powerhouse in functionality. I really miss the days when an MP3 player just played music. After a near fatal fall of my phone (luckily just the screen protector cracked!) it became important that an expensive phone might not be the best thing to lug around while performing yardwork. This excellent device solves that issue, and solves it well.

Songs and MP3 audio books were loaded easily onto the player. It is not made by Apple nor is part of their line, so the iTunes program does not work with this. However, it is a easy fix - just go to your Music folder on your computer, and drop the files you wish into this device's memory. Easy peasy and quick. It comes with an included 32 GB of memory, but can easily be upgraded if you install your own micro SD card, up to 128 GB.

It comes with wired earphones, which I did not use or test. With the invention of easy to pair Bluetooth earphones, I have no desire to be ever tethered with a headphone cord again. The player pairs easily with all 3 of my Bluetooth devices - earphones, headphones, and speakers. The sound from each device is flawless, which might be a function of the device, but is also determined by the source.

There are just 3 buttons on the side of this MP3 player - on/off button, volume up, and volume down. All other functions are controlled by the small but well designed touch screen. It is very comparable with the touch capability of modern phones, the programs are opened with ease and operate in an intuitive logical manner. There are other functions built into this device, but since I really got it as an MP3 player, that is what I am focused upon.

With this player comes a handy removable back clip, letting you clip it on/in a pocket, armband, belt, anywhere. Without the clip, it is small enough to easily slip into any pocked of your cloths, even the tiny change pockets in most jeans. Besides the wired earphones & clip, there is a 3mm audio cable for attaching it manually to another device, and a Micro USB cable for charging. There is a plastic protective film on the front face - it can be removed, but the touch screen operates just fine if it is left on.

This is my new favorite toy, It it not cheap or flimsy, but in all honesty, looks and feels like a tiny cell phone in how its constructed. It does not happen often, but this wonderful MP3 player exceeded my expectations.
text_fidelity_b: FDY MP3 Player, MP3 Player with Bluetooth5.0, 32GB Portable Music Player with FM Radio/Recorder, HiFi Lossless Sound Quality, 2.4Inch Touch Screen Mini MP3 Player for Running, Expandable 128GB TF

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR Nighthawk 4-Stream AX4 Wi-fi 6 Router (RAX40) – AX3000 Wireless Speed (Up to 3 Gbps) | 1,500 Sq Ft Coverage Bought this router a few days ago and have already begun the return process. I didn't have a good gut feeling about this router from the start, partly because the reviews are not all raves and partly simply because it looks kind of...evil to me. I am definitely not a fan of the hyper-aggressive router design trend that seems to be targeted at adolescent male gamers. I do not look at this thing and think it looks cool and feel positive feelings; I look at it and feel...apprehension. As a physical object, it's not something I really want in my apartment. But I decided to give it a try anyway because I don't think that kind of gut feeling should be one's primary consideration in choosing a router, and because I often like having the latest, cutting-edge tech and thought it would be nice to be ready for Wifi 6 for when I eventually get an iPhone 11 or some other device that features that protocol. But unfortunately, the negative experiences do not come only when I look at the thing.

I was at first alarmed, as I set up the router, by what a very long time it took anything to happen in the app. At every point at which I so much as switched to a different screen in the app, both during and after setup, the app would chug for an alarmingly long time before finally displaying the page I'd navigated to. This is to be expected when the router needs to restart, but...these were not points at which the router needed to restart. These were not points at which I'd changed any setting at all. These were points at which nothing at all had happened except that I'd attempted to go from, say, the app's main page to the Device Manager page, or the Wifi Settings page, or wherever. Simply switching pages in the app would take 20 or 30 seconds or longer. Another negative first impression.

I also noticed that the app doesn't give me access to a lot of the features of the router I expect to have access to. Granted, I'm an advanced user compared to a lot of people - networking is an aspect of computing I've enjoyed mucking around in for decades now, and my inclination with a new router (or an old one, for that matter) is to dive straight into areas of the settings where many ordinary users may fear to tread. But the Nighthawk phone app appears to be targeted more toward the average consumer. Which, if you're more the average consumer, is fine. But if you're me, you find that to be a disappointing restriction.

Then I started trying to use the web UI instead, and while it gave me access to all those more techy parameters I sought, I found the same delay problem happening when I tried to switch from one page of settings to another, but here it happened for longer, and sometimes the target page wouldn't load at all until I clicked again, this time on the blank page with the spinning progress indicator in the center.

So both of the means I have for interfacing with the router are inordinately slow, and one of them is clunky and glitchy on top of it.

And finally, add to all this the way I will occasionally go to navigate to any ordinary webpage and be told my browser can't display the page because I'M NOT CONNECTED TO THE INTERNET, and voila! - the straw that broke the proverbial camel's back.

This happens, and I go and look at the router to see if maybe it's restarted itself for some reason (automatic software update?) and...no. All lights are on and looking as they do during normal operation; the router's just not providing said normal operation.

I never once had such problems with the Apple AirPort Extreme I replaced with this router, nor with the Linksys AC5400 I bought more recently and then wound up giving to a friend. So, because I want a router that, unlike the AirPort Extreme, is tri-band, is still supported with software/firmware updates, and might also feature better performance with multiple connected devices, I bought myself another AC5400 with which I will be replacing this unsatisfactory Netgear thing as soon as it arrives.

And also because I decided I can wait for Wifi 6 until such time as I actually do have devices capable of taking advantage of it, which may be quite some time (i just bought a new MacBook Pro which doesn't support it, and I don't see the iPhone 11 as having any compelling advantages over my iPhone XS Max, soooo...).

The Linksys AC5400 is a monster among 802.11ac routers and has garnered much respect in tech mags and blogs and so forth. Plus I myself have about a year's experience with one and it's been fast, reliable, and glitch-free. So if you're looking for a new router and don't feel compelled to buy into 802.11ax just yet (few devices support it yet anyways), I heartily recommend that one.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Nighthawk 4-Stream AX4 Wi-fi 6 Router (RAX40) – AX3000 Wireless Speed (Up to 3 Gbps) | 1,500 Sq Ft Coverage

The WPS light kept flashing and eventually timed out with no 5Ghz signal. Not a problem, had to login to the interface via the built in webpage and connect to the 5Ghz hotspot manually. But in the end, I ended up disabling 5G on the extender to router side because it was actually slowing the connections down because the 5Ghz band has a harder time going through walls than the 2.4Ghz band. Overall, this range extender works as well as one can hope for the 22 dollars it cost. Was able to expand the indoor range of the router's signal by at least 50 feet in a brick, wood and stucco house.

Innergie mCube Mini 90 Watt Auto/Air Power Adapter and 10W USB Output (TADP-90AB AA) - White I wanted this power adapter for one reason only, to keep my Kindle Fire running on road trips, and it works for that purpose. It connects by plugging into the cigarette lighter; it does not come with an AC plug. The device is nicely packaged in a stretchy black carry bag (the right size for my Kindle Fire, actually) with a pull-cord closure and comes with an additional small bag containing ten interchangeable tips to give flexibility in fitting the power port of various laptops. If one of the free tips does not work with your laptop, you can contact the company to obtain a free specialty tip, but I do not know what the shipping cost might be.

I have a 13" MacBook Pro with a MagSafe power adapter, so of course none of the tips would be usable for charging my laptop in the car. At 90W, the Innergie may be capable of charging my Mac with a USB charging cable, but I'm not going to buy one to find out because I never take my laptop in the car with me. (I hope anyone who does and has tested the mCube 90 with their Mac will post a comment here.)

As far as my Fire is concerned, at first I thought I needed to get a custom tip, and Innergie responded quickly to let me know that one that small was not available. Then it occurred to me that I could perhaps use my old Kindle 2 USB charging cord with the USB port of the mCube, but I was nervous about trying it. I wrote Innergie, and they responded that one of the people in the office used this method for charging their Fire with no problems. So it will get the job done.
text_fidelity_b: Innergie mCube Mini 90 Watt Auto/Air Power Adapter and 10W USB Output (TADP-90AB AA) - White

text_fidelity_a: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White So... I own both the tower and now several dots.  Of course the dots are more reasonably priced, however, the speaker ability is really where it's vastly different.  Obviously the tower is much better in the speaker department.  However, I did find that there is a cordless speaker you can buy to go with your 2nd gen dot that is an improvement and still at lower price point than the tower when combined with the cost of the dot. (Mokcao cordless speaker - amazon sells it too) Because the dots are so reasonably priced we have them in all 3 major rooms and use the cordless speaker to drop one dot in and take it outside to our sunroom when we like.  Over all, I am pleased with both my tower AND dots... but probably will stick to dot purchases in the future because of the price point.  I would say if you've been on the fence, the dot is well worth a try.  It's very easy to set up, you will need to download the app, also easy to follow step by step setups.  Once you're hooked up you will be amazed at how often you use Alexa.  At our house she helps me keep track of where I am supposed to be every day... timers... night time meditation... the occasional argument and even plays games with us as well as much needed comedic relief.  It may not be "necessary" to have Alexa, but I am always surprised at how often we use her assistance.  It's nice and worth it to us.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

Belkin Verve Folio Case with Stand for Samsung Galaxy Tab 10.1inch (Black) My favorite types of cases are the rigid style that grab onto the edges of the device and do not increase the width or length of the device significantly. This is sort of a hybrid between that style and Belkin's ultrathin folio style.

That's because this one has a "pocket" for the device just like the soft ultrathins, which means you see the screen through a well placed cutout. It also has holes cut for the buttons, lenses, and ports. It is smaller from a length and width perspective than the ultrathin, but a bit deeper because the cover is thicker. It also has cleaner lines, although not as clean as some hard cases.

It also has an elastic strap attached to the cover that can be turned around to hold the case shut. Only time will tell if that stays nice and tight or ends up sagging after use. Really, it doesn't need to be used often as the case will mostly stay shut by itself.

The one thing I don't like is the way you fold the front cover behind the back: it sort of seems too stiff, as if you're not really supposed to. It also folds at both joints, which keeps it from lying completely flat. The ultrathin folio has it beat in that case, although I like the Verve in better in most other ways.

A nice case for your tablet.

ONANOFF Fokus Headphones, Premium Concentration Over-Ear Headphones, Designed with Two Unique Listening Modes: FokusMode and MusicMode, Adjustable, Built-in Mic, and Passive Noise Cancellation, Grey I'm so happy to see they are still making new brands of wired headphones... lately all the new designs and features have been found in wireless only, and sometimes I just want a good pair of wired 'phones, especially for use with my Quad-DAC headphone jack.
They are passive noise cancelling, which basically just means they cushion sound out mechanically with nice big ear muff style rings, as opposed to any kind of digital reverse-sine-wave trickery (which are hit or miss on cheap brands usually), and it has a really interesting "focus" mode switch, which changes the EQ of the mix to promote the frequencies used in spoken words better. This is an amazing feature for those of us who listen to audiobooks or lectures, which I do frequently. To be honest, I didn't notice a big difference between having that mode on and off, but it was nice to know someone out there is trying to make products catered for people who want to do more than just listen to music over Bluetooth.
The sound quality is pretty good for the price, and the presentation is actually really impressive. The materials feel really premium and even the box it comes in feels super fancy, which might make this a nice gift. I don't expect much out of mics that are embedded in headphones, and this pair didn't change my mind about that. The mic isn't close enough to your mouth to be of much use, picking up more ambient noise around you than you. If they wanted to include that as a feature, they could have made a removable arm like a gaming headset, but they don't need to. This is a good pair of headphones for those of us who just want to listen, which is their ideal demographic IMO.
text_fidelity_b: ONANOFF Fokus Headphones, Premium Concentration Over-Ear Headphones, Designed with Two Unique Listening Modes: FokusMode and MusicMode, Adjustable, Built-in Mic, and Passive Noise Cancellation, Grey

text_fidelity_a:
LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports A good laptop chiller pad becomes important when you run a lot of graphics-intensive games or if you are doing anything requiring the CPU to run a heavy load. Heat is the enemy of a computer system and the fastest way to a dead laptop is to not deal with heat issues when there’s a problem. I had a chill pad some time ago and it was sub-par. This one by LotFancy is much better and it does a good job.

First off, this is a big chill pad, the same basic dimensions as my laptop but much thicker. I have a 15.6" laptop and this pad is almost a perfect and exact fit, with only a narrow area in the back that extends past the end of the laptop. If you want a small and petite chill pad, this is not the one you want. It does incline too with a metal bar and slots in the case so that the laptop can be angled up. This actually is good for exposing it to even more air.

This chill pad connects to a USB port so it can either be plugged into a port on the computer or into a hub. There are two ports on it and both seem to be the same in terms of how the pad operates. That is, the pad operates at the same speed regardless of which port is used. There are also two buttons on the pad for turning it on. One turns on the larger fan in the middle, and the other turns on all the other fans. Two green LEDs next to those buttons indicate that the pad is powered on and working.

This pad moves a lot of air and it does a good job of cooling the laptop. But, it does so very quietly which is a huge plus. I have it set up in my home office and the pad makes about as much noise as a desktop computer, maybe a little less. The sound it makes is a gentle hum.

When powered on each fan has a bright blue LED in it. While they look cool when there’s no laptop on the pad, they’re all but invisible when the laptop is sitting on top. There isn’t even much of a glow coming from the pad. I turned on the pad, turned out all of the lights and the glow from the laptop screen was enough to overpower any light that might have come from the pad. Except for the low hum I wouldn’t know it was even turned on.

This is a good chill pad. It works quietly and it moves a lot of air. Compared to other chill pads I have used this one is very good and I am happy to recommend it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2) Prior to receiving this review sample I was happy with in-ear type phones, but always grabbed headphones when I wanted to listen to music without disturbing others, These phones changed that. For one thing they are super comfortable. For another the sound is incredible. In fact I have been testing various phones - mainly from this brand, but also some Sennheiser models - and this is head and shoulders above the pack.

I'll be honest and disclose that comfort edges out sound when phones sound good enough. I will normally not quibble over a few hundred Hz one way or the other as long as I can wear the phones without noticing them. These are not only unobtrusive, but downright comfortable, which is a major reason why these have now replaced my trusty [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]].

Soundwise the specs do not begin to describe the richness, especially bass. In fact, when I read the 20 Hz to 20 MHz range I thought that the sound would be somewhat generic for phones in this range. I own a pair of IEMs (in-ear monitors) that go as low as 18 Hz at the same 95dB at 1mW sensitivity, yet these sound much deeper than those. I love the balance of sound across the frequency spectrum as though it's on a smooth continuum. Every one of my test albums I played through these phones sounded so good that I decided that it's time to hang up the headphones and go with these.

Part of the reason why I love these from a comfort perspective is the over the ear memory wire. I prefer that style, but not everyone does. They are definitely stiff and take on a shape that will be uniquely yours over time (and a very short time at that!) Also, while this ships with a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] the phones will not fit after you have contoured them to your ear. The case is useful for carrying around the array of adapters and tips that are included. In fact, the final reason I love these phones is the included triple-flange style silicon tips, which block out the rest of the world and allow me to focus solely on music.

If you love music and want to hear every note faithfully reproduced in their natural frequencies these phones are it. I can honestly say that I have not used a better set of phones from any brand in this price range, including some Sennheiser models that have a street price of fifty to seventy-five dollars more than these, so the value is definitely there.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)

Diamond Multimedia 300Mbps 802.11n Wireless Repeater Range Extender with Wireless Access Point and Wireless Bridge Device (WR300NSI) This wireless range extender was fairly easy to install. The directions were straight forward, and the device was up and running in less than fifteen minutes. It comes with an CD, but we didn't have to use it. We did have to reset the IP address on the computer, but that may have a user issue and not related to the device itself.

It took a little while to find the best place to plug the device in based on our home's layout, but we found one that worked. In our house plan, the best place ended up being in the hallway at baseboard level. Fortunately, the device is small and plugs straight into the wall, eliminating any unsightly cords. It would have been nicer to have the device a little more out of the way. We were a little concerned about this thinking it might get kicked or knocked by the kids as they race around and play. That hasn't happened yet, but it is something to take into consideration if you have small children or pets around. We tried placing it in a less open area hoping to protect it a little more, but none of those areas produced a satisfactory result.

It's very easy to tell how much of a signal the device is receiving from the main router. Three bars is full signal, and one is low signal. The signal indicator light is easy to read and is quite bright. Since the device is in our hallway, it acts as a nice night light and would be rather distracting if it were in a bedroom.

The end result: the dead spots are gone. We can use all of our devices in the those areas without having to worry about losing a signal.

Avantree DG40SA Dedicated Windows 10 Bluetooth USB Adapter, Wireless Dongle for PC Bought with Win 10, Plug & Play, Support Headpones, PS4 Gaming Controllers, Mouse, Keyboard, Printers etc. I purchased a Lenovo Ideacentre AIO Y910 in December 2017 and it had a beautiful built-in Qualcomm bluetooth function. It worked great. I had my desktop paired with my Echo Dots and with Alexa could continue listening to movies/music/podcasts/youtube anywhere in my house away from the computer. Along came a Windows 10 update in March 2018 that disabled/removed the bluetooth function/drivers ENTIRELY. No roll backs/restores, or reinstallations brought it back. The internal bluetooth function was completely ruined and prevented from running. I was furious and microsoft support was zero help. I finally begrudgingly purchased this to do the same function. I'm angry I had to pay for something I already paid for my computer to have, and that I have to waste a USB spot for it, but it works, was truly plug and play, though the connecting of all my speakers/Echo Dots is more complicated that previously. For example, with the original bluetooth capabilities, I could chose to have one or both of the Dots automatically connect when bluetooth was enabled. I could have them play together or verbally tell Alexa to connect/disconnect. Now for some reason with this bluetooth, voice control doesn't work, Alexa can't disconnect (she will do it but then it automatically reconnects) and if one Dot is connected the other won't. I have to run back to my computer's bluetooth settings and pair/unpair and connect/disconnect each time I want to make a change. This is frustrating. If anyone knows of anyway to circumvent this or the original bluetooth death please let me know, I'd be forever grateful.

The range for the device is fine, I live in a 1200 sq ft two story townhome and there was no issue with my computer seeing the Dot in the bedroom or the Dot downstairs. Connections are strong.
